title: Chocolate peppermint truffles
subtitle: dark chocolate ganache truffles with a clean mint finish
excerpt: Chocolate peppermint truffles are dark chocolate ganache, lightly scented with peppermint extract and rolled in cocoa powder. The ganache chills overnight, then is scooped and rolled by hand into balls. The whole batch takes about fifteen minutes of active work and a few hours of chilling.
sourceNotes: Classic ganache truffle method, widely documented in British confectionery manuals and cookery books from the mid-twentieth century onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth emulsion of chocolate and hot cream. The ratio of chocolate to cream determines whether the ganache is used as a glaze (thin), a truffle filling (medium), or a firm rolled truffle (thick).

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer, then transfer to a freezer bag. Defrost overnight in the fridge and roll in cocoa before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before serving.

content.text: The key to a smooth truffle is a stable

: hot cream poured over finely chopped chocolate and left to melt before stirring. Stirring too early or too vigorously splits the emulsion and makes a greasy ganache. Use 70% dark chocolate for the best depth against the peppermint.
Place the finely chopped dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Heat the double cream in a small saucepan over a medium heat until it just comes to the boil, then pour it immediately over the chocolate.
Leave undisturbed for 2 minutes, then stir from the centre outward in slow circles until a smooth, glossy ganache forms.
Add the butter and stir until fully incorporated. Stir in the peppermint extract. Taste and add a little more extract if needed, bearing in mind the flavour intensifies as the ganache chills.
Cover the surface of the ganache with cling film pressed directly onto it and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until firm enough to scoop.

Sift the cocoa powder onto a plate. Using a teaspoon or melon baller, scoop pieces of ganache roughly 2 cm across and roll quickly between lightly cocoa-dusted palms into a ball. Work fast: the warmth of your hands softens the ganache.
Roll each truffle in the cocoa powder until evenly coated. Transfer to a lined tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving or boxing up.

attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring before the cream has had time to melt the chocolate, and avoid over-stirring.
attrs.fix: If split, add 1 tablespoon of warm cream and stir gently from the centre; this sometimes recovers a split ganache.

attrs.problem: Truffles are too soft to roll
attrs.avoid: Avoid working with ganache that has not chilled long enough.
attrs.fix: Return the ganache to the fridge for a further hour or place briefly in the freezer for 20 minutes.
